summary: A three-player Russian trick-taking game with marriages and auction where players race from 501 down to zero.
rules_text: A 24-card deck (A,10,K,Q,J,9) is used. Card points are A=11, 10=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2, 9=0. Each player is dealt 7 cards, 3 cards form a face-down talon. Players bid clockwise starting left of dealer; minimum 66, must raise, two passes end it. Bids may be blind with cards face-down for double score. The highest bidder takes the talon, now with 10 cards, announces a final contract at least as high as the winning bid and chooses trumps or no trump, then gives one face-down card to each opponent, leaving 8 cards each. Alternatively the bidder may resign and lose the bid amount while opponents lose 25. Left of dealer always leads. Must follow suit; if void must trump if possible. Highest trump, or highest of led suit if no trump, wins the trick. Leading K or Q while holding both of a suit declares a marriage: 40 in trump, 20 otherwise (20 all suits if no trump). Marriage counts only if declarer wins a trick. After 8 tricks, if bidder met contract, subtract contract from his score, else add it; opponents subtract their trick points. Opponents at 100 or less cannot score as defenders. First to 0 or below wins.
